quote: According to Arif Habib Ltd Head of Research Tahir Abbas, headline inflation in September is likely to settle at 25.3pc, with the year-on-year price increases led by food (29.5pc) and transport (63.9pc) sectors.

“With July 2024 CPI now further expected to cool down to 10.5%, despite a MoM uptick of 1.6%, Pakistan’s real interest rate (RIR) remains at sky-high levels, further expanding to 10 percentage points,” said JS Global in a report on Saturday.

However, brokerage firm AKD Securities projected inflation to drop to 0.84% year-on-year in March 2025, marking the lowest rate in the last six decades, largely due to deflation in food, housing, and transport costs.
The brokerage house shared that with inflation expectations of 6.5-7.0% for September 2025, real rates will surge to 400-450bps [basis points], higher than Pakistan’s historic average of 200-300bps.
